final_rationale: The Actor did not provide genuinely new admissible evidence. The response mostly narrows and reframes the same record: aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support launch context, but the admissible summary still shows an unresolved claims-triage weakness, an incomplete draft mitigation artifact, and a disclosure conflict in the model-card draft. That reframing is more policy-bounded than the original clean-certification position, but it does not cure the core compliance gap because the caveat itself is an unresolved compliance predicate. Under the stated policy, certification without material caveats requires either evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation. If the weakness is material and unresolved, disclosure is required unless covered by approved risk acceptance. The record provided here does not show that the required disclosure was actually made or approved, and it does not show approved mitigation or risk acceptance. So the strongest admissible conclusion remains that current certification is not yet compliant on this record.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence resolves the unresolved below-target claims-triage weakness in a named launch use case.
No approved mitigation or risk-acceptance record is identified with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion.
The proposed caveat path depends on explicit limitation disclosure, but no evidence shows the final model-card disclosure was updated or approved.
The draft model-card statement that there are no known material limitations remains in tension with the reviewer comment and the unresolved slice issue.
Aggregate readiness and a clean rehearsal remain supportive but do not satisfy the policy predicate on their own.
